Hopkins. I guess I know him but I'm not sure now
Do you have his address? Walter?
No Well, it's Leroy Thompson's too. I'm not sure I have his address. I used to have it but a lot of people move around
Yeah, we have to meet and move around and do it in St. Philip now, see
So, we'll
But all of us can get in for you
Yeah, we'll go get those addresses from you Well, if there's nothing else then to add, we'll turn it off We'll certainly enjoy talking to you and hearing you play those two numbers too

segments.title: Interview setup at Piku's bar; birth in Verrettville, 1904
segments.summary: Russell opens the interview at Piku's bar on October 6; Nelson gives his name and says he was born March 21, 1904 in Verrettville, St. Bernard Parish, with an older brother.

segments.title: Starting guitar at eight; brother Henry 'Stacks' Nelson
segments.summary: Nelson taught himself a six-string at eight, moved to the city at about ten, and says his older brother Henry Nelson, called Stacks, also played guitar.

segments.title: Building the bazooka with Noon; playing for Pat O'Brien and Walter Coquille
segments.summary: Nelson, Noon (Edward Johnson) and others played two guitars and a bazooka made from hose; they played for Pat O'Brien, went to Florida, and worked with Walter Coquille on radio.

segments.title: First paid jobs: Kiddo's band, Silver Star and the St. Claude band
segments.summary: Nelson's first job was with Kiddo's band at the Silver Star; later he worked with Herbert Moran and in a band on St. Claude with George Lewis, a woman pianist and drummer Richard Hall.

segments.chapter: Uncle Gaiye and New Orleans bands
segments.title: His uncle Gaiye (Butler Rap) and the Fern or Budweiser dance hall
segments.summary: Nelson describes his uncle, a banjo, guitar and trombone player who worked with Chris Kelly and Sam Morgan and was killed at the Fern/Budweiser dance hall on Burgundy.

segments.chapter: Uncle Gaiye and New Orleans bands
segments.title: Playing guitar and bass with Chris Kelly's band
segments.summary: Nelson recalls playing in Chris Kelly's band, where Johnny St. Cyr and Kid Rena were also heard; he names bassist Cleo and says he played guitar, banjo and some bass.

segments.chapter: Uncle Gaiye and New Orleans bands
segments.title: Getting an electric guitar before the war
segments.summary: Nelson got an electric guitar shortly before the last war and sold it to a man called Mr. Cubby.

segments.title: Learning from his uncle, his brother and Milano
segments.summary: His uncle and brother gave him tips; he studied about six months with Milano, who had no method book and showed chords on his horn, and Nelson played by ear.

segments.title: Favorite guitar players, playing blues, not singing
segments.summary: Nelson cannot recall the names of the guitarists he followed, says he mostly played blues, and never sang, having others sing for him.

segments.title: Composing blues in a dream: Walter's Special and Walter's Lullaby
segments.summary: Nelson makes up blues as he plays and describes dreaming a new melody, getting up to play it; the result became Walter's Special and a slow dance tune, Walter's Lullaby.

segments.title: Playing at Boscoville and with Leroy King's group
segments.summary: Nelson says he plays at Boscoville that weekend and describes how to get there and the players, including Leroy King and a bassist.

segments.title: Trumpeter Blue (Walter Robinson) and whether he has given up music
segments.summary: Russell and Nelson talk about trumpet player Blue, Walter Robinson, who served in the army and seems to be slacking off from lack of regular playing.

segments.title: Playing for Piku at the bar and earlier on London Avenue
segments.summary: Nelson has played Saturdays with Mr. Piku for about six years and in bands with him over 25 years; they were earlier at a London Avenue place that opened in 1952.

segments.title: Alamaster Street job and the fire that destroyed his guitar and amplifier
segments.summary: Nelson played a short time at Luton's on Alamaster Street with Blue, pianist Sammy and a drummer; a fire destroyed the drum and his guitar and amplifier, which he had to replace.

segments.title: Touring Nashville and failed audition records with Lira's blues group
segments.summary: Nelson says he went around Nashville with friends, and that a group with Blue and Lira singing blues cut six audition records on Claiborne and Desire but never heard back.

segments.title: His sons Walton and Lawrence, who play drums and guitar
segments.summary: Nelson says both sons, Walton and Lawrence, play music and taught themselves drums and guitar.

segments.title: How Piku's music was played in the old days
segments.summary: Nelson says Piku's style was the same, but they never used a band, just two guitars in the backyard at parties.

segments.title: Piku's brother, the Creole singer who played kazoo
segments.summary: Nelson plays kazoo and two guitars on many jobs with Piku's brother, who made up his own Creole songs and played only the kazoo.

segments.title: Rudy Doody's and the gypsy tea room
segments.summary: Nelson and Collins place Rudy Doody's at Sanana and Robinson and distinguish it from the gypsy tea room, where rooming houses now stand.

segments.title: The song 'A La Ba' and the Creole language
segments.summary: Nelson first heard 'A La Ba' sung by Billy and Dee Dee; Burbank recorded it; Nelson knows no Creole despite coming from St. Bernard.

segments.chapter: Down in St. Bernard and the uncle
segments.title: Life in rural St. Bernard: flooded roads, the dance hall, Tom Albert and Paul Mugnier
segments.summary: Nelson describes the town where people traveled by boat, the dance hall with musicians brought in by boat, and musicians such as Tom Albert and Paul Mugnier from there.

segments.chapter: Down in St. Bernard and the uncle
segments.title: What bands his uncle played in and his instruments
segments.summary: Nelson says his uncle played with Punch, Sam Morgan and Guy Kelly, switching between banjo, guitar, trombone and alto horn, and preferred guitar; he never learned electric guitar.

segments.chapter: Down in St. Bernard and the uncle
segments.title: When his uncle died and his reputation among musicians
segments.summary: Nelson places his uncle's death before the war, during the Depression, and Russell says people like George Guesnon call him a wonderful musician.

segments.chapter: Down in St. Bernard and the uncle
segments.title: The uncle's origins and being a sideman; Nelson's childhood curfew
segments.summary: Nelson says his uncle came from Verrettville, had no other musical relatives, mostly played with others, and whipped him for staying out late as a boy.

segments.chapter: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
segments.title: The uncle's last job at the Budweiser and his age
segments.summary: Russell and Nelson confirm that the Budweiser was the uncle's last job and that he was about twenty years older than Nelson.

segments.chapter: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
segments.title: His first guitar, a cheap one bought by his father
segments.summary: Nelson's first guitar was a cheap, funny little instrument his father brought him in the country at age eight, and his small hand could only finger half of it.

segments.chapter: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
segments.title: His brother Henry 'Stanks' Nelson
segments.summary: Nelson says his brother played in bands mostly in Raceland, died about twenty years ago, and was known as Stanks.

segments.chapter: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
segments.title: Request to hear him play a number
segments.summary: Russell and Collins ask Nelson to play something, perhaps the dream tune, and Nelson goes to get his guitar.

segments.chapter: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
segments.title: Uncle's full name: Butler Rap, nicknamed Gaiye
segments.summary: Nelson says his uncle's name was Butler Rap, nicknamed Gaiye, and no one knows what the nickname means.

segments.chapter: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
segments.title: Guitar demonstration and finger-and-thumb playing
segments.summary: Nelson plays his dream tune on guitar; asked about his style he says he uses finger and thumb and the rest is garbled.

segments.chapter: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
segments.title: Teaching local kids and his weekend gigs
segments.summary: Nelson says kids come around to learn and explains he plays Friday and Sunday but stays home Saturday, though others want him to work.

segments.chapter: Second reel: instrument, style and wrap-up
segments.title: Getting addresses for Walter Blue and pianist Sammy Hopkins; closing
segments.summary: Russell asks for addresses of Blue, Sammy Hopkins and Leroy Thompson to arrange future interviews, then thanks Nelson and closes the reel.
